title: flightctl-helper trusted configuration v2 (root-owned allowlist)
description: NEW in round 3 (Sol 6 C7h finding). The privilege boundary of the root helper, as data the helper reads from ONE fixed root-owned path. The caller (executor account) can pass no config path, no environment and no free-form argument: every subcommand argument must match this allowlist. Install invariants (checked by the C7h install audit, tests/contracts_v2/validation.py helper_install_audit/sudoers_audit): the helper executable, this config and every directory up to / are owned by root and not writable by group or other; sudo has exactly ONE rule for the executor account, NOPASSWD, naming the helper's absolute path, with env_reset and no SETENV; managed keys live in a root-owned directory referenced by sshd AuthorizedKeysFile (never in the friend's home, so no attacker-controlled path or symlink is followed) and are written with O_NOFOLLOW to a temp file in that directory then renamed.

caller_account.description: The only account sudo lets run the helper (the executor account).

argv_roots.description: argv[0] of unit-start must resolve (realpath) under one of these root-owned directories; no shell.

agent_isolation.description: Round 5 (Sol 6 r4): agents' unit work runs with systemd DynamicUser=yes, one ephemeral UID per job unit, and StateDirectory=flightctl-jobs/<job_id> with StateDirectoryMode=0700. systemd keeps DynamicUser state directories under a root-only (0700) private parent, so another agent job (another ephemeral UID) cannot traverse to or read this job's staging; the shared fc-svc account is gone. The helper records the job's UID from the running unit (systemctl show -p UID) and output-collect accepts only files owned by that UID. output-collect takes the job id only and resolves the recorded UID (round 6).

claims_dir.description: Root-owned 0700 directory on PERSISTENT storage (never tmpfs: a claim must survive reboot until reconciled); one <account>.parent file per active friend parent lease.

operator_account.description: Round 8 (Sol 6 r7): the only account whose sudo-started invocation of /usr/local/libexec/flightctl-claim-clear may lift a quarantine. Must differ from caller_account and from every friend account (helper_config_semantics). Its sudoers rule must re-authenticate (no NOPASSWD): operator_sudo_audit. Round 9: that rule must also set timestamp_timeout=0 for the program (clear_fresh_auth_audit).

x-subcommands.unit-start: agents: --job <public id> --lane <lanes key> --unit <unit_name_pattern> -- <argv>  => systemd-run (system manager) -p DynamicUser=yes -p StateDirectory=flightctl-jobs/<job> -p StateDirectoryMode=0700 -p DevicePolicy=closed -p DeviceAllow=<lane nodes> -p KillMode=control-group --collect; friends: --account <friend_accounts> --parent-lease <lease_id> (ONE admission rule (round 8): while the account is quarantined, no claim of any kind is admitted (no new parent, no child of the old parent); otherwise a request is admitted only as the account's first parent claim or as a child of the claimed parent; the claim check and systemd-run run under the account's flock) and --uid=<account> instead of DynamicUser
x-subcommands.unit-stop: --unit <unit_name_pattern>  (only units this helper started: checked by the unit's FLIGHTCTL_HELPER=1 property)
x-subcommands.session-open: --account <friend_accounts> --parent-lease <lease_id> --lane <lanes key> --pubkey-file-fd 0 --expires <utc>: ONE admission rule (round 8): while the account is quarantined, no claim of any kind is admitted (no new parent, no child of the old parent); otherwise a request is admitted only as the account's first parent claim or as a child of the claimed parent. The first parent claim is published with an atomic link(); the claim check and the session setup run under the account's flock, which claim-reconcile also takes to write the marker
x-subcommands.output-collect: --job <public id>  (round 6: no account argument. The helper resolves the job id in its root-owned job registry, written at unit-start, to the job's unit and the UID recorded from that unit (systemctl show -p UID right after start: the per-job DynamicUser UID for agents, the fc-<name> UID for friends). After the unit stopped and its cgroup is empty it copies from that job's staging only regular files with st_nlink == 1 and st_uid == the recorded UID into the executor-owned output store, and rejects the rest.)
x-subcommands.claim-release: --account <friend_accounts> --parent-lease <lease_id> + close proof (user slice empty, lane occupancy empty, keys removed): the ONLY way a claim is removed. Race-safe: open the claim O_NOFOLLOW, check the lease, rename it to a unique tombstone, and delete only if the tombstone's inode equals the opened fd's inode; otherwise restore it and refuse. Refused while the account is quarantined (only the operator's claim-clear lifts a quarantine)
x-subcommands.claim-reconcile: --active <account=lease_id,...> --boot <boot id>: called during A8 reconcile. NEVER removes a claim: a claim the authority lists is 'kept'; one it omits is 'orphaned-quarantined' and one naming another parent is 'conflict'; both write the account's quarantine marker, which REFUSES every later session-open/unit-start for the account (children of the old parent included), under the account's flock, and raise an operator alert; NOT a way to clear: see x-operator-clear

x-operator-clear: Round 8 (Sol 6 r7): claim-clear is NOT a subcommand of the executor's helper (which refuses the name). It is the separate program /usr/local/libexec/flightctl-claim-clear --account <friend_accounts> --parent-lease <lease_id> + close proof, mode 0700 root:root, so only root can execute it, reachable only through the operator's own sudoers rule '<operator_account> ALL=(root) /usr/local/libexec/flightctl-claim-clear' WITHOUT NOPASSWD and with FRESH authentication on every invocation: 'Defaults!/usr/local/libexec/flightctl-claim-clear timestamp_timeout=0' (round 9, Sol 6 r8: sudo otherwise accepts a cached credential for 5 minutes; sudoers(5) 1.9.17p2: 0 = always prompt, command-specific Defaults are applied once the command's path is known; `!authenticate` is forbidden; config/flightctl-claim-clear-sudoers.example). It refuses unless its real and effective UID are 0 and SUDO_USER/SUDO_UID (set by sudo after env_reset) equal operator_account and its UID (clear_authorized). It takes the account's flock, removes the claim (inode-checked tombstone) and then the marker; a crash in between leaves the account blocked. The C7h install audit runs operator_sudo_audit on `sudo -l -U <operator>` (every route to the program, including ALL, wildcard, directory, regex, argument-bearing and Cmnd_Alias grants, must be password-protected, and the EFFECTIVE timestamp_timeout for the program must be 0) and no_clear_route_audit (the same route matching) for the executor and every friend account; both also read the installed sudoers files to expand Cmnd_Alias, and an unresolvable alias counts as a route (fail closed).
